intro: This library is reviewed against primary sources, not secondary summaries. 12 changes in the last ninety days, from the state bill tracker, the federal agency watch and the framework explainers, newest first.

items.body: Montana has no dedicated AI act, but its 2025 legislature passed the Right to Compute Act, government-AI limits, and deepfake laws, while a 1973 consumer protection law and 2023 genetic privacy act already reach AI conduct.
items.headline: Montana AI Laws

items.body: The state-by-state AI laws now in effect. Impact assessments, transparency, employment-decision rules, voice-and-likeness rights, consumer notification.
items.headline: State AI Laws

items.body: Nevada has no omnibus AI act, but 2025 brought a real mental health AI restriction, an election deepfake disclosure law, and enforcement reach through existing privacy and consumer protection statutes.
items.headline: Nevada AI Laws

items.body: Puerto Rico has no dedicated AI act. Its flagship AI framework bill has stalled and its AI institute was vetoed, but narrower laws on election deepfakes, image cloning, and government AI transparency have passed, layered onto existing consumer protection, data breach, and constitutional privacy law.
items.headline: Puerto Rico AI Laws

items.body: Wyoming has no dedicated AI act, but a 2026 law criminalizes AI-generated child exploitation material, and existing consumer protection, data breach, and insurance statutes already reach AI-driven conduct in the state.
items.headline: Wyoming AI Laws

items.body: Arkansas has no dedicated AI act, but its 2025 session passed five AI-specific laws on deepfakes, AI-generated CSAM, publicity rights, and government AI use, and older consumer, privacy, and insurance statutes already reach AI conduct.
items.headline: Arkansas AI Laws

items.body: The Justice Department’s Antitrust Division filed a proposed consent decree today to resolve the United States’ claims against Pinnacle Property Management Services LLC, as part of its ongoing enforcement action in the Middle District of North Carolina against algorithmic ...
items.headline: DOJ: Justice Department Reaches Proposed Consent Decree with Pinnacle, One of America’s Largest Landlords, to Resolve Information Sharing and Algorithmic Coordination Claims

items.body: The Federal Trade Commission extended by seven days the public comment period on the proposed enforcement policy statement regarding personalized pricing View Press Release
items.headline: FTC: FTC Extends Public Comment on Proposed Policy Statement Regarding Personalized Pricing

items.body: The Securities and Exchange Commission’s Investor Advisory Committee will host a public meeting at the SEC Headquarters in Washington D.C. on Sept. 10 at 10 a.m. ET to discuss artificial intelligence technologies in the public markets and the SEC’s…
items.headline: SEC: SEC Investor Advisory Committee to Host Sept. 10 Meeting

items.body: The Federal Trade Commission finalized orders requiring Cox Media Group (CMG) and two other firms to pay a total of $930,000 to settle allegations they deceived customers by falsely claiming to offer an AI-powered service that could target localized ads based on conversations ...
items.headline: FTC: FTC Finalizes Orders with Cox Media Group, Two Other Firms Settling Charges They Deceived Customers About “Active Listening” AI-Powered Marketing Service

items.body: Utah requires generative AI to disclose it is not a person, enforced by the Division of Consumer Protection with fines to $2,500 per violation. Amended in 2025 to narrow the general duty to high-risk interactions, with a stricter always-on rule for regulated occupations.
items.headline: Utah AI Policy Act

items.body: The federal agencies actively enforcing existing laws against AI misuse. Anti-AI-washing, disparate impact, adverse action, registrant governance.
items.headline: Agency Enforcement
